blocks.text: Design a food delivery platform like Swiggy, Zomato, or DoorDash, connecting a customer, a restaurant, and a delivery partner around a single order. This project's ride-hailing design already solved matching a rider directly to a nearby driver the instant both are ready to go. Food delivery is a genuinely different coordination problem: an order passes through a restaurant's own preparation time first, and the entire experience depends on dispatching a delivery partner not merely to the nearest available one, but to whichever partner's arrival will line up with the exact moment the food actually becomes ready, since either extreme, a partner waiting idle or food sitting and cooling, is a real, visible failure.

blocks.alt: An accepted order's predicted ready time drives dispatch of whichever available delivery partner will arrive right as the food is actually ready

blocks.text: The technique that solves this is dispatch-timing optimization, predicting how much longer an order needs to finish preparing and choosing, among available nearby partners, whichever one's own travel time to the restaurant most closely matches that remaining prep time, minimizing both wasted partner idle time and food quality loss.

blocks.text: A customer should be able to place an order with a restaurant and track its status through preparation, pickup, and delivery. A restaurant should be able to accept an order and signal its preparation progress. The system should dispatch a delivery partner timed to arrive close to when the order actually becomes ready, not simply the nearest available partner regardless of timing. A partner already assigned to an order should not be assigned a second, unrelated one at the same time, unless it is a deliberately compatible batched trip. A delivery should be verifiably completed before payment to the delivery partner is finalized.

blocks.alt: Well-timed dispatch, efficient batched deliveries, correct partner assignment, food arriving while still good, and verifiable, honest delivery completion

blocks.text: Well-timed dispatch means a partner dispatched too early sits waiting idle at the restaurant, while one dispatched too late leaves food cooling before it even leaves, and the design has to actively minimize both. Efficient batched deliveries mean a single partner's trip can sometimes efficiently cover more than one nearby order rather than always dedicating one partner per order. Correct partner assignment means a busy partner already committed to one order must never be double-assigned to an unrelated second one. Food arriving while still good is really the ultimate point behind well-timed dispatch, quality on arrival is the actual product outcome being optimized for. And verifiable, honest delivery completion means a delivery marked done should genuinely reflect food actually reaching the customer, not merely a partner's own unverified claim.

blocks.text: This design assumes geospatial candidate discovery for nearby delivery partners reuses the same location-indexing approach this project's other location-based designs use, and focuses instead on what is genuinely new here, dispatch timing and batching. A restaurant's remaining prep time is assumed predictable from its recent order history and current queue depth, refreshed regularly rather than recomputed from scratch on every single order. Batching is assumed in scope, a partner already en route can take on a second, nearby order if the added detour is small enough not to meaningfully delay either delivery.

blocks.text: A platform at real scale might see millions of orders placed per day across many cities, served by hundreds of thousands of active delivery partners at any given moment. A dispatch decision has to happen within seconds of an order being accepted by the restaurant, since every additional second of delay pushes the eventual partner-arrival-versus-food-ready timing further off. A meaningful share of trips can be efficiently batched with a second nearby order, reducing the total number of partner trips needed relative to a strict one-partner-per-order model.

class DispatchResult:
    # The outcome of a dispatch decision: which partner was chosen, and how
    # much "waste", the mismatch between their travel time and the food's
    # ready time.
    def __init__(self, partner_id, waste):
        self.partner_id = partner_id
        self.waste = waste


class DispatchService:
    # Chooses, among currently available partners, whichever one's own travel
    # time to the restaurant best matches an order's predicted remaining prep
    # time, minimizing wasted partner idle time or food cooling time.
    def __init__(self):
        self.travel_time_minutes_by_partner = {}  # partnerId -> ETA to restaurant
        self.busy_partners = set()

    def register_partner(self, partner_id, travel_time_minutes):
        self.travel_time_minutes_by_partner[partner_id] = travel_time_minutes

    def dispatch(self, order_id, remaining_prep_minutes):
        best_partner_id = None
        best_waste = float('inf')

        for partner_id, travel_time in self.travel_time_minutes_by_partner.items():
            if partner_id in self.busy_partners:
                continue  # excluded: already assigned elsewhere

            waste = abs(travel_time - remaining_prep_minutes)  # how far off arrival is from food-ready time
            if waste < best_waste:
                best_waste = waste
                best_partner_id = partner_id

        self.busy_partners.add(best_partner_id)  # mark this partner busy, excluding them from future dispatches
        return DispatchResult(best_partner_id, best_waste)


def main():
    dispatch_service = DispatchService()
    dispatch_service.register_partner("partner-A", 15)  # 15 minutes travel time to this restaurant
    dispatch_service.register_partner("partner-B", 10)  # 10 minutes travel time
    dispatch_service.register_partner("partner-C", 30)  # 30 minutes travel time, far away

    # Order 1: 12 minutes of prep remaining.
    result1 = dispatch_service.dispatch("order-1", 12)
    print(f"Order 1 (prep remaining 12 min) dispatched to: {result1.partner_id}, waste={result1.waste} min")

    # Order 2: 20 minutes of prep remaining. partner-B is now busy from order 1.
    result2 = dispatch_service.dispatch("order-2", 20)
    print(f"Order 2 (prep remaining 20 min) dispatched to: {result2.partner_id}, waste={result2.waste} min")

    print("partner-B correctly excluded from order 2 (already busy):", result2.partner_id != "partner-B")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Capacity: millions of orders per day across many cities, hundreds of thousands of active partners, and dispatch decisions needed within seconds.

The core techniques: dispatch-timing optimization minimizing partner-arrival-versus-food-ready mismatch, and partner exclusivity, both worked through with a real, verified implementation in Java, Python, and C++.
Database: a zone-partitioned, near-real-time partner availability index alongside an order store carrying a live, periodically-updated prep-time estimate.
End-to-end workflows: a normal dispatch flow and a partner-cancellation redispatch flow, both traced as sequence diagrams.
Consistency: a strongly consistent, exclusive partner assignment per order paired with a best-effort, approximate prep-time and arrival prediction.

Trade-offs: dispatch-timing optimization versus dispatching the nearest partner immediately versus waiting until food is fully ready, compared directly on partner idle time and food quality on arrival.
